title: Flashcard apps compared: Lucida, Anki, Quizlet and more
description: Compare Lucida with Anki, Quizlet, Knowt, RemNote, Brainscape, Mochi, Kahoot and Gizmo on price, spaced repetition, AI and importing, with dated sources.
h1: Lucida compared with other flashcard apps
lead: These pages compare Lucida with Anki, Quizlet, Knowt, RemNote, Brainscape, Mochi, Kahoot and Gizmo on price, spaced repetition, AI, importing, sharing and games, with a source and a date for every fact. Each page says plainly where the other app is better.

bullets: **Full control, add-ons and offline study:** Anki. It is free on computers and Android, and [Lucida vs Anki](https://lucida.cards/vs/anki) shows the trade-offs.
**The biggest library and teacher tools:** Quizlet. See [Lucida vs Quizlet](https://lucida.cards/vs/quizlet) for what its free plan covers.
**AI built into the app:** Knowt, RemNote, Brainscape, Mochi or Gizmo. Their free plans limit it. Lucida’s own AI makes cards too, up to 3 makes a day on Free.
**Notes and cards in one place:** RemNote. See [Lucida vs RemNote](https://lucida.cards/vs/remnote).
**Markdown, local-first and offline:** Mochi. See [Lucida vs Mochi](https://lucida.cards/vs/mochi).
**Expert-made decks and a simple 1 to 5 rating:** Brainscape. See [Lucida vs Brainscape](https://lucida.cards/vs/brainscape).
**Live games for a school or event:** Kahoot. See [Lucida vs Kahoot](https://lucida.cards/vs/kahoot).
**A quick start in a browser, cards made from your files or by your own AI, and free Learn mode and live games:** Lucida.

paras: Lucida is new, and these pages say where it is behind:
bullets: No App Store app yet. It runs in a browser on computers and phones.
No offline mode. It needs an internet connection.
No add-ons and no custom card templates.
It can’t read Anki .apkg files, only Anki’s plain-text export, and pictures, sounds and review history don’t come across.
Its library of shared decks is new and much smaller than Quizlet’s or AnkiWeb’s.
Live is multiple choice, for individuals, with up to 60 players, and you host it from a computer.
It doesn’t make cards from a web page address. You can paste the text or save the page as a PDF.

paras: Every fact about another app comes from its own site, help pages, privacy policy or app store listing, opened on September 30, 2026. Where we couldn’t confirm something, we left it out. Prices are as of September 2026 and can change. Facts about Lucida come from the app, its pricing page and its privacy policy, and are as of October 1, 2026.
If you find a mistake, write to team@lucida.cards and we will fix it.

faq.q: What is the best flashcard app?
faq.a: It depends on what you need. Anki is best for control, add-ons and offline study. Quizlet is best for a huge library and teacher tools. Knowt, RemNote, Brainscape, Mochi and Gizmo each build in AI in different ways. Lucida is for a quick start in a browser with cards made from your files or by your own AI, plus free Learn mode and live games.

faq.q: Anki vs Quizlet: which is better?
faq.a: Anki is built for long-term memory and control: it is free on computers and Android, works offline and has more than 1,600 add-ons. Quizlet has a huge library of shared sets, teacher tools and live games, and limits Learn and Test on its free plan. Pick Anki for control and long-term study, and Quizlet for shared sets and use in school.

Anki supports FSRS, RemNote offers FSRS 6 as a beta option, Mochi lets you switch to it, and Lucida plans reviews with FSRS by default. Brainscape uses its own confidence system, and Quizlet, Knowt, Kahoot and Gizmo don’t say which algorithm they use.

All of them have a free plan, with different limits. Anki is free on computers and Android (its iPhone app is $24.99). Lucida’s core is free. Mochi is free, local and offline. Brainscape is free for your own text cards. Quizlet, Knowt, RemNote, Kahoot and Gizmo are free with limits on learn modes, AI, player counts or daily use.

faq.q: Which flashcard apps have AI built in?
faq.a: Quizlet, Knowt, RemNote, Brainscape, Mochi (on Pro, with small free amounts), Gizmo and Kahoot (paid tools) have AI built in, usually with monthly or daily limits. Anki gets AI through add-ons. Lucida has AI built in for making cards from your files, pictures, recordings, YouTube links or a topic (3 makes a day on Free, 30 on Pro), and your own AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP app) can also make and edit cards through your Lucida link.

faq.q: Which flashcard apps can import Anki decks?
faq.a: RemNote and Mochi import Anki .apkg files with review history. Gizmo imports an Anki deck through Magic Import. Brainscape takes Anki’s text export, Knowt takes Anki decks through a spreadsheet paste, and Lucida reads Anki’s Notes in Plain Text export.

Anki and Mochi work offline. RemNote’s desktop and mobile apps do, Brainscape’s mobile apps do once you download your cards, Quizlet’s mobile apps can study Flashcards and Match offline, and Kahoot’s app has an offline mode. Lucida has no offline mode. We couldn’t confirm it for Knowt or Gizmo.

faq.q: Which flashcard apps have live games?
faq.a: Kahoot is built for live quiz games. Quizlet has Classic Quizlet Live, Knowt has Knowt Play, Gizmo has Gizmo Live, and Lucida has Live for up to 60 friends on any deck. We found live games in none of Anki, RemNote, Mochi or Brainscape.

Lucida is a flashcard app that runs in the browser at app.lucida.cards. It plans every review with FSRS spaced repetition, makes cards from your files, pictures, recordings, YouTube links or a topic, and lets your own AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP app) make and edit your cards through your personal Lucida link. The free plan has unlimited decks and cards, Learn mode, sharing, live games and 3 card makes a day. Pro is $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year.
Yes, in the browser. Open app.lucida.cards in Safari. There is no App Store app yet.
